system: You are the Planner of a nonprofit-finance theory-testing pipeline. You turn a theory into a JSON test spec in the exact format shown. You choose variables, the expected sign, the unit the exposure is assigned to and controls; you never compute a statistic. The validation gate (alpha, effect floor, permutations, hold-out) is fixed by the pipeline and replaces whatever you write. Use only the column names listed. Reply with one JSON object and nothing else.
prompt:
Theory: Nonprofits in counties where families spend more of their income on housing carry more debt relative to what they own.

Scout mapping: {"outcome": "liabilities_to_assets", "exposure": "avg_housing_burden", "exposure_type": "continuous", "exposure_unit": "county_fips", "controls": ["log_revenue", "return_type", "category", "state", "tax_year", "median_household_income", "poverty_rate", "unemployment_rate"], "notes": "Debt relative to assets is liabilities_to_assets, and the county housing-cost burden (avg_housing_burden, a continuous county-year measure) is the exposure; controls cover organization size, form type, sector, state, year, and county economic conditions that may confound the link, with return_type restricted to 990 filers for ratio theories."}

Example spec for a binary exposure (follow this format exactly):
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "theory_id": "ratings_fairness",
  "theory": "Standard financial-ratio ratings unfairly penalize nonprofits in high-need counties.",
  "source": "docs/ratings_theory.md",
  "written_by": "hand (CP3); from CP4 the Planner agent writes specs in this format",
  "outcome": "standard_rating",
  "exposure": "high_need",
  "expected_sign": -1,
  "exposure_unit": "county_fips",
  "exposure_varies_by": "tax_year",
  "population": {
    "return_type": ["990"],
    "require_true": ["has_county", "has_need"],
    "require_present": ["standard_rating", "high_need", "log_revenue", "category", "county_fips"]
  },
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "claim": "The mean standard rating is lower in high-need counties than elsewhere.",
      "method": "difference_in_means"
    },
    {
      "id": "H2",
      "claim": "The gap remains after controlling for organization size (log revenue), sector (NORP category) and tax year.",
      "method": "fixed_effects",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category"],
      "cluster": "county_fips"
    }
  ],
  "robustness": [
    {
      "id": "H2_multilevel_2022",
      "method": "multilevel",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "categorical": ["category"],
      "group": "county_fips",
      "years": [2022]
    },
    {
      "id": "H2_county_year_means",
      "method": "two_stage_group_means",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category"],
      "groups": ["county_fips", "tax_year"]
    }
  ],
  "validator": {
    "alpha": 0.05,
    "effect_floor_sd": 0.1,
    "n_permutations": 999,
    "seed": 6235,
    "permutation": {"keep_paths": true, "studentized": true},
    "holdout": {"by": "state", "folds": 5},
    "holdout_year": 2022,
    "outcome_rule": {"heavy_tail_ratio": 3.0, "winsorize": [0.01, 0.99]}
  }
}


For exposure_type "continuous", set hypotheses H1.method to "correlation". Use the Scout's outcome, exposure, exposure_type and exposure_unit unchanged. Give a fresh theory_id (snake_case).
text:
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "theory_id": "housing_burden_leverage",
  "theory": "Nonprofits in counties where families spend more of their income on housing carry more debt relative to what they own.",
  "source": "scout mapping (housing burden and nonprofit leverage)",
  "written_by": "planner agent",
  "outcome": "liabilities_to_assets",
  "exposure": "avg_housing_burden",
  "exposure_type": "continuous",
  "expected_sign": 1,
  "exposure_unit": "county_fips",
  "exposure_varies_by": "tax_year",
  "population": {
    "return_type": ["990"],
    "require_true": ["has_county"],
    "require_present": ["liabilities_to_assets", "avg_housing_burden", "log_revenue", "category", "county_fips", "state", "tax_year", "median_household_income", "poverty_rate", "unemployment_rate"]
  },
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "claim": "Liabilities-to-assets is positively correlated with county average housing burden.",
      "method": "correlation"
    },
    {
      "id": "H2",
      "claim": "The positive association remains after controlling for organization size, county economic conditions (median household income, poverty rate, unemployment rate), and absorbing sector, state and tax year.",
      "method": "fixed_effects",
      "controls": ["log_revenue", "median_household_income", "poverty_rate", "unemployment_rate"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category", "state"],
      "cluster": "county_fips"
    }
  ],
  "robustness": [
    {
      "id": "H2_multilevel_2022",
      "method": "multilevel",
      "controls": ["log_revenue", "median_household_income", "poverty_rate", "unemployment_rate"],
      "categorical": ["category", "state"],
      "group": "county_fips",
      "years": [2022]
    },
    {
      "id": "H2_county_year_means",
      "method": "two_stage_group_means",
      "controls": ["log_revenue", "median_household_income", "poverty_rate", "unemployment_rate"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category", "state"],
      "groups": ["county_fips", "tax_year"]
    }
  ],
  "validator": {
    "alpha": 0.05,
    "effect_floor_sd": 0.1,
    "n_permutations": 999,
    "seed": 6235,
    "permutation": {"keep_paths": true, "studentized": true},
    "holdout": {"by": "state", "folds": 5},
    "holdout_year": 2022,
    "outcome_rule": {"heavy_tail_ratio": 3.0, "winsorize": [0.01, 0.99]}
  }
}
